details: Found 30 Oct by the trial of relay on a copy of relay cleaned of relay (owner, 30 Oct: "Полагаю что для текущих задач будет не лишним проверить подключение relay к самому relay, очищенному от relay"); sandbox HOME, RELAY_HOME and RELAY_PROJECTS, claude stubbed. setup wrote the shared .claude/settings.json with extraKnownMarketplaces pointing at the absolute path /Users/amidman/relay, 'openspec@amidman': false, and permissions allow Bash(kit:*), Bash(bin/kit:*), Bash(relay:*); the file is committed for the whole team, the path is this Mac's, and setup's Done list mentions none of it.
failing_case: `relay setup` in a fresh repo: .claude/settings.json contains '/Users/amidman/relay' and three Bash permissions; the Done list names none.
pass_cases: the committed settings.json holds no absolute path
the Done list names each permission added
a project with its own settings.json keeps its entries
reason: tests/test_setup_off.py t1b (no absolute path, Done names additions) fails at base, passes at head.
findings.summary: setup commits an absolute relay path into settings.json

details: CONFIRMED by reading docs/setup.md lines 15-16 at HEAD; the change did not touch docs. The doc is the description of setup's promise,
and now contradicts the very fix (Principle 10: a newcomer does the task from the program's own texts). Size: 5 minutes.
evidence: - `.claude/settings.json`: the relay marketplace and the plugins for the
$ git diff --stat master...HEAD   -> no docs/ file
failing_case: Read docs/setup.md at HEAD, the list of what `relay setup <dir>` writes: "`.claude/settings.json`: the relay marketplace and the plugins
for the flow (...), `Bash(kit:*)` allowed". After this change setup writes no marketplace there (it removes an old one) and allows three
rules: Bash(kit:*), Bash(bin/kit:*), Bash(relay:*). A newcomer reading the doc expects the marketplace in the committed file.
fix_hint: Rewrite the first line of that bullet: "`.claude/settings.json`: the plugins for the flow (...), and `Bash(kit:*)`, `Bash(bin/kit:*)`,
`Bash(relay:*)` allowed, each named in the done list; no marketplace path (it is the machine's, in ~/.claude/settings.json), and an
old one an earlier setup wrote is removed and said."
pass_cases: docs/setup.md, the .claude/settings.json bullet, says the marketplace is not written there (it lives in ~/.claude/settings.json via `relay setup --global`) and that an old directory entry of relay's marketplace is removed and said in the done list.
The same bullet names the three permissions Bash(kit:*), Bash(bin/kit:*), Bash(relay:*), and that the done list names each one it adds.
The "Nothing in ~/.claude" bullet stays as it is (it already says the marketplace is the user's file).
findings.summary: docs/setup.md still says setup writes the relay marketplace into .claude/settings.json and allows only Bash(kit:*)

details: CONFIRMED by reading settings_additions: `key not in plugins(before) and value is False`. The brief asks for every permission and setting
setup *added*; a changed value is beyond the letter, hence LOW, but it is the same trust problem the trial found (a committed file
evidence: lib/relay_setup.py:402-403: lines += [... for key, value in plugins(after).items() if key not in plugins(before) and value is False]
failing_case: merge_settings sets openspec@amidman to false (remove=turned_off), but settings_additions skips it (key already in before), and the
plugins line lists only the enabled ones. Done says nothing about openspec being turned off in the committed file. Expected: a line
fix_hint: Also emit a line for a key whose value differs between before and after (before[key] is not after[key]).
pass_cases: {"enabledPlugins": {"openspec@amidman": true}} + `--specs none` -> one Done line names openspec@amidman turned false.
Fresh repo, `--off gopls-lsp@claude-plugins-official` -> Done still has "added openspec@amidman = false" once (t1b) and no line for a key already false.
Second run with nothing changed -> no settings_additions line (t2 stays).
reason: tests/test_setup_off.py test_f2_a_switch_flipped_true_to_false_is_named_in_done (fails at base) and test_f2_a_key_already_false_gets_no_line pass.
findings.summary: Done names a switch only when the key is new; a relay key setup flips from true to false (specs turned off) is still silent

details: CONFIRMED by reading: .claude-plugin/marketplace.json name is "amidman"; the wrapper (last changed 21 Oct, before the 28 Oct rename)
still reads `.relay`. Outside this change (untouched), but it is the one reader of the marketplace path this change now makes the only
home of it. Works on the owner's Mac only because relay sits at ~/relay. Size: 15 minutes (read the name from marketplace.json or try both).
failing_case: Relay checked out at /opt/relay, `relay setup --global` run (user settings hold extraKnownMarketplaces.amidman.source.path = /opt/relay),
RELAY_ROOT unset, no ~/relay. A session's `relay ...` on PATH runs the wrapper: jq '.extraKnownMarketplaces.relay.source.path' is empty,
root = ~/relay, and it fails "relay: repository not found". Expected: it runs /opt/relay/bin/relay.
fix_hint: Look up .extraKnownMarketplaces.amidman (or the name read from the marketplace file next to the wrapper), keeping the RELAY_ROOT and ~/relay fallbacks.
pass_cases: User settings with extraKnownMarketplaces.amidman.source.path = <dir with bin/relay>, RELAY_ROOT unset -> the wrapper execs <dir>/bin/relay.
RELAY_ROOT=<dir> set -> it uses RELAY_ROOT regardless of settings.
No settings file and ~/relay present -> falls back to ~/relay.
reason: Kind outside, wrapper untouched; goes to a fix item. Agree with the fixer.
findings.summary: the relay wrapper looks up extraKnownMarketplaces.relay, but the marketplace is named amidman since 28 Oct, so it always falls back to ~/relay
